name: Contact Form Email
author: codepeople

sections.description:
Contact Form to Email features:

► Email delivery & notifications    
► Direct email reply with free AI assistant (no API key required)
► Saves messages into database
► Export to Excel / CSV
► Printable list of messages
► Visual drag and drop form builder 
► Anti-spam captcha 
► Field validation
► Printable reports
► One-click contact form
► Classic and AJAX submission available
► Automatic email reports
► Supports GDPR-compliant forms
► ... and more features (see below)

Contact Form to Email is a powerful and easy-to-use WordPress plugin to create contact forms, send their data to email addresses, and reply directly from the admin dashboard with AI assistance.

Contact Form to Email also saves the contact form data into a database, provides printable reports, and includes the option to export selected data to CSV/Excel files.

Contact Form to Email Main Features:

  • Direct Email Reply with AI Assistant: Reply to bookings and contact messages directly from the WordPress admin messages list. Includes a built-in, free AI assistant to automatically draft polite, context-aware responses in seconds—with no API key or external account required.
  • Email delivery / notifications: The contact form data is sent by email to one or more email addresses. It also supports configuring auto-replies to the user who filled out the contact form.
  • Form data saved into the database: Avoid losing submissions and keep a complete record of received contact form messages.
  • Printable list of messages: View the list of messages received from the contact form within a selected date range and print it.
  • Export data to CSV/Excel: Export contact form data to a standard format that can be used by other applications. Export email addresses and other contact form data using date and text search filters.
  • Automatic reports: Generate automatic reports of contact form usage and submitted data, including daily submission reports, cumulative hourly reports, and printable reports for specific fields to help you understand your data.
  • Automatic email reports: Send automatic reports to specified email addresses on a regular schedule.
  • Form validation: Set validation rules for each contact form field to keep your data clean.
  • Anti-spam protection: Built-in captcha anti-spam protection. No need to rely on external services for contact form anti-spam protection.
  • Drag and drop contact form builder: An intuitive contact form builder for customizing form fields and validation rules.
  • Customizable email messages: Specify the text of the contact form email notifications. Supports both plain text and HTML-formatted emails.
  • Multi-language support: The contact form builder allows you to enter field labels and validations in any language, with full support for special characters.
  • Classic and AJAX submission: After clicking the submit button, the user can be redirected to a “Thank You” page, or a “Thank You” message can be displayed on the same form page without refreshing it. This can be configured in the settings.
  • Enable/Disable notifications: Both email notifications to administrators and email confirmations to users can be optionally enabled or disabled from the settings area.

Contact Form to Email – More Features

There are also commercial versions of Contact Form to Email with additional features available at https://form2email.dwbooster.com/download

The commercial version can be converted into a payment form or booking form with integration for multiple payment gateways: PayPal Standard, PayPal Pro, Stripe, Authorize.net, Skrill, Mollie / iDEAL, TargetPay / iDEAL, SagePay, RedSys TPV, and Sage Payments. Payments are SCA-ready (Strong Customer Authentication) and compatible with the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2).

The commercial version also features an ultra-powerful visual form builder, file upload fields, conditional logic, multi-page forms, WooCommerce integration, Mailchimp integration, Clickatell and Twilio SMS integration, iCal attachments, signature fields for signing with a mouse or directly on touchscreens, and more.

Contact Form to Email Messages List

The messages list helps you review past contact form submissions, reply directly to users, and print or export records. It includes a search/filter form with the following options:

  • Search for: Search for specific text within the contact form messages.
  • From … To: Date range to include in the list and reports.
  • Item: If you have more than one contact form, select whether to view results from a specific contact form or from all forms.
  • Filter: Displays the list according to the selected filters and options.
  • Export to CSV: Exports the CSV data according to the selected filters and options.

Each message in the list includes quick action buttons:

  • Reply (with AI Assistant): Opens a reply modal pre-filled with the user’s email address and original submission. You can type brief instructions (e.g., “Confirm the booking for Tuesday at 10 AM”) and click Generate with AI to draft a complete reply using a free, keyless AI service. Sent replies are automatically appended to the message record for easy tracking.
  • Edit: Modify the stored submission data.
  • Delete: Remove individual or marked submissions.

The exported CSV file contains a header row with the field names, followed by one contact form submission per row, with one form field in each column. This allows you to easily import the data into other applications or select only the columns/fields you need (for example, selecting only email addresses). A CSV file can be opened and managed directly in Excel.

The list of contact form messages is shown below the search area. A Print button below the list formats the messages into a printer-friendly view.

The Contact Form Reports

The reports section lets you analyze the usage of your contact forms and the data entered into them. The first section contains a filter bar similar to the one on the messages list page. Below the filters, three graphical reports are available:

  • Submissions per day: Displays a line graph showing how many contact form submissions were received each day within the selected date range. This report can be used to evaluate contact form peaks and measure the impact of marketing campaigns.

  • Submissions per hour: Displays a line graph showing how many contact form messages were received during each hour of the day across all messages in the selected date range. This report helps identify peak hours so you can focus support resources accordingly.

  • Report of values for a selected field: Select any contact form field or metadata field (such as date, IP address, or hour) to see how many times each value has been entered or selected. This is very useful if your form is used as a poll to gather feedback, making it easy to generate reports on selectable fields and better understand your customers’ profiles and needs.

A Print button at the bottom of the page lets you print the value report for the selected contact form field in a printer-friendly format.

Automatic Email Reports

The Contact Form to Email plugin supports two types of automatic (periodic) email reports:

  • Global Email Reports: Configured below the list of forms. This option sends a report containing new submissions across all forms every specified number of days.

  • Form Email Reports: Configured on the settings page of each individual form. This option sends a report containing new submissions for that specific form every specified number of days.

Reports are attached as a CSV/Excel file to the emails. In both cases, you can specify the destination email addresses, email subject, email text, and report interval. More information is available in the “Other Notes” section.

Language Support

The Contact Form to Email plugin is compatible with all character sets. The troubleshoot area contains options to change the encoding of the plugin database tables if needed. Multiple translations are already included in the plugin.

Form Builder & AI-Assisted Replies

The plugin includes a visual drag-and-drop form builder to add, modify, and delete text fields, textareas, and email fields with their respective validations, plus an AI-assisted email reply system directly inside the bookings/messages list.
Replying to contact form messages with AI: Go to the “Messages” section and click the “Reply” button next to any submission. A modal window will open with the recipient’s email address and original message pre-loaded. You can optionally enter brief instructions in the AI Assistant Instructions box and click Generate with AI to automatically compose a response without needing an API key, then click Send Reply.

Opening the contact form messages in Excel: Go to either the “Reports” or “Messages” section and click the button labeled “Export to CSV”. CSV files can be opened in Excel—just double-click the downloaded CSV file, and it will display the selected contact form submissions, one per line.

Deleting a contact form message: Go to the “Messages” section and use the “Delete” button for the contact form message you want to delete. Each row in that list represents a contact form submission.

Getting the contact form email from the user: The “From” address used is a fixed email address specified in the contact form settings, which helps prevent emails from being classified as spam. However, when you click “Reply” in your email client, the user’s email address will appear automatically as the recipient because the Reply-To header is set for this purpose.

Customizing the captcha image: The captcha image used in the contact form is 100% implemented inside the plugin, so you don’t need to rely on third-party services or servers. In addition to the settings for customizing the captcha design, you can also replace the font files located in the contact-form-to-email/captcha/ folder.

Contact form email format: Notification emails sent from the contact form can be either plain-text or HTML emails. Plain-text emails are preferred in most cases since they are easier to edit and are more likely to pass anti-spam filters.

Contact form Clone button: The Clone button duplicates a complete contact form along with its settings. The contact form messages/emails and statistics are not duplicated.

Custom contact form submit button

There is a settings section in each form that allows you to specify the label of the submit button.

The class="pbSubmit" selector can be used to modify the button styles.

The styles can be applied in any of the CSS files of your theme or added in “Contact Form to Email > Customization area > Add Custom Styles” (at the bottom of the page that contains the list of forms).

For further modifications, the submit button is located at the end of the file cp-public-int.inc.php.

For general CSS style modifications and examples, check this FAQ entry: https://form2email.dwbooster.com/faq#q82

Customizing the automatic email reports

The settings for the email reports (both global and per-form reports) include the following configuration fields:

  • Enable Reports?: Option for enabling or disabling the reports.
  • Send report every: Indicate how often (in days) the reports will be sent.
  • Send after this hour (server time): Approximate time at which the reports will be sent, based on server time. Some site activity is needed to trigger report delivery, or you can set up a cron job for exact delivery timing.
  • Send email from: The “From” email address used for the reports. Avoid @aol.com and @hotmail.com “From” addresses to prevent anti-spam filtering issues.
  • Send to email(s): The list of email addresses (comma-separated) that will receive the reports.
  • Email subject: Subject of the email sent with the Contact Form to Email reports.
  • Email format?: Format of the email sent with the reports (HTML or Plain Text). In most cases, plain text is easier to set up and encounters fewer issues with anti-spam services.
  • Email Text (CSV file will be attached): Content of the email that will contain the Contact Form to Email reports. The reports will be attached in CSV format.

The contact form database

The messages received via the contact form are stored in the WordPress database table wp_cftemail_messages. You can export that data as automatic email reports or in CSV/Excel format from the messages list area. If needed, you can also query that table directly for further processing of the contact form data.

Importing messages

There is an option to import messages into the Contact Form to Email plugin, located below the messages list and labeled “Import CSV”.

Messages can be imported from a comma-separated CSV file: one record per line, one field per column. Do not use a header row with the field names.

The first 3 columns in the CSV file are the time, IP address, and email address. If you don’t have this information, leave the first three columns empty. After those initial columns, the fields (columns) must appear in the same order as in the form.

Sample format for the CSV file:

2013-04-21 18:50:00, 192.168.1.12, john@sample.com, "john@sample.com", "sample subject", "sample message"
2013-05-16 20:49:00, 192.168.1.24, jane.smith@sample.com, "jane.smith@sample.com", "other subject", "other message"

“From” address used for the emails

In the “Form Processing / Email Settings” section, the first setting is named Send email “From” and has the following options:

  • From fixed email address indicated below – Recommended option: If you select “From fixed…”, the customer’s email address will appear in the “To” address when you hit “Reply”. This is the recommended setting to avoid mail server restrictions.

  • From the email address indicated by the customer: If you select “From customer email”, the customer’s email will appear visually as the sender when you receive the email, but this is not supported by all hosting providers and can trigger spam filters, so it is not recommended in most cases.

The drag and drop contact form builder

The Form Builder lets you add, edit, and remove fields in the contact form and specify validation rules (required fields, email fields, etc.).

The following field types are currently available in the version published in the WordPress directory:

  • Single Line Text: Classic one-line text input.
  • Email: Validates that the email address has a valid format.
  • Paragraph Text: Classic multi-line (textarea) text input.

In other versions of the plugin, the following fields are also available: Numeric field with specific validations, Date-picker, Checkboxes, Multiple Choice Radio buttons, Dropdown / Select, Upload file fields, Password, Phone with specific validations, static texts, section breaks, and page breaks for multi-page contact forms.

Other features in the contact form builder:

  • Equal fields validation: Use it, for example, to confirm that the email or text typed in two different fields is identical. Valid for “Single Line Text” and “Email” fields.

  • Dependent fields: Use this feature to show/hide fields (any field type) based on the selection made in other fields (checkboxes, radio buttons, or select/drop-down fields). This feature isn’t fully available in this version since the related selection fields aren’t included.
sections.installation:
To install Contact Form to Email, follow these steps:

  1. Download and unzip the Contact Form to Email plugin.
  2. Upload the entire contact-form-to-email/ directory to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  3. Activate the Contact Form to Email plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  4. Configure the contact form settings under Settings > Contact Form to Email.
  5. To insert the contact form into a page or post, use the block or editor icon when editing content.
sections.faq:
Where do I report security bugs found in this plugin?

Please report security bugs found in the source code of the Contact Form to Email plugin through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. The Patchstack team will assist you with verification, CVE assignment, and notifying the developers of this plugin.

Q: Do I need an API key or paid account to use the AI Reply Assistant?

A: No. The AI Reply Assistant in the messages list works out of the box using a free, keyless AI service. You do not need to register for an external account or enter an API key to generate email replies.

Q: How can I add specific fields into the email message?

A: There is a tag named <%INFO%> that is replaced with all the information submitted from the contact form. However, you can also use optional tags for specific fields in the contact form.

To do this, click the desired field in the form builder and look for the read-only setting named “Field tag for the message (optional):”. Copy and paste that tag into the contact form email message text; after form submission, the tag will be replaced with the text entered in that form field.

The tags have this structure (example): <%fieldname1%>, <%fieldname2%>, <%fieldname3%>, …

More info and supported tags at https://form2email.dwbooster.com/faq#q81

Q: Can I add a reference to the item number (submission number) into the email?

A: Yes. Use the tag <%itemnumber%> in the email content. That tag will be replaced by the contact form submission item number.

Q: I’m having problems with non-Latin characters in the contact form.

A: Use the “Troubleshoot Area” to change the character encoding. Try the UTF-8 option first.

Q: I’m getting this message: “Destination folder already exists”. What is the solution?

A: The free version must be deleted before installing the pro version.

If you are uploading a new version via Plugins > Add New > Upload and a previous version is still installed, delete the previous version first. This is a safe step; the plugin’s data and settings will not be lost during the process.

Another alternative is to overwrite the plugin files through an FTP connection. This is also a safe step.

Q: How do I edit or remove the form title / header?

A: In the form builder within the administration area, click the “Form Settings” tab. That area allows you to edit the form title and header text, as well as choose different alignments for the field labels.

Q: Can I align the form horizontally in two or more columns?

A: In the form editor, click a field and locate the setting named “Add Css Layout Keywords”. In that field, enter the name of a CSS class that will be applied to the field.

There are predefined CSS classes to align two, three, or four fields on the same line:

column2
column3
column4

For example, if you want to place two fields on the same horizontal line, specify the class name column2 for both fields.

Q: What does each field in the contact form settings area mean?

A: For each contact form, you can edit the following settings:

Form Processing / Email Settings:

  • Send email “From”: Indicates whether the email will be sent from a fixed email address or from the email address entered by the customer. This is explained in more detail in the “Other Notes” section.
  • “From” email: The email address used as the “From” address in notifications (when using a fixed “From” address).
  • Destination emails (comma separated): List of administrators who will receive the email notification.
  • Email subject: Subject of the notification email sent after form submission.
  • Include additional information?: Optional information about the user’s IP address and browser.
  • Thank you page (after sending the message): After submitting the form, the user can be redirected to a page on your website (usually a “Thank You” page). Enter the page URL in this field.
  • Email format?: Select whether the email will be sent as plain text or HTML-formatted.
  • Message: Content of the notification email that you will receive after each submission of the contact form. Keep the tag <%INFO%>, which will be replaced automatically with the form data sent by the user.

Form Builder: The drag-and-drop contact form builder. It is explained in detail in the “Other Notes” section.

Submit Button: Specify the label of the contact form submit button (no need to add it manually from the visual contact form builder). Also contains settings and instructions for further customizing the submit button and form CSS styles.

Validation Settings: Contains the text strings used for contact form validations. You can easily translate them into other languages.

Email Copy to User:

  • Send confirmation/thank you message to user?: Select whether you want to send a confirmation/thank-you message to the user.
  • Email field on the form: Select the field that contains the user’s email address on the contact form.
  • Email subject: Subject of the confirmation email sent to the user.
  • Email format?: Select whether the email will be sent as plain text or HTML-formatted.
  • Message: Content of the confirmation email sent to the user. The tag <%INFO%> will be replaced by the information submitted through the contact form.

Captcha Verification:

  • Use Captcha Verification?: Select whether a captcha image will be used on the contact form to prevent spam.
  • Width: Width of the captcha image.
  • Height: Height of the captcha image.
  • Chars: How many characters will appear in the captcha image.
  • Min font size: Minimum font size used (randomized).
  • Max font size: Maximum font size used (randomized).
  • Preview: Preview for checking how the captcha image will look.
  • Noise: Amount of noise to make the captcha stronger.
  • Noise Length: Length of the noise lines to modify its appearance.
  • Background: Background color.
  • Border: Border color.
  • Font: Base font used to render the text (four options included).

Automatic Reports (Send submissions in CSV format via email): Contains settings to automatically send reports at a specified interval containing the data of all contact forms submitted during that period. Report settings are explained in detail under “Other Notes” (see “Customizing the automatic email reports”). Note: All submissions are stored in the contact form database, so they can be easily recovered when needed.

Q: Can I get the URL of the page where the form was displayed before submission?

A: Yes, you can add the tag <%referrer%> to the email content, and it will be replaced with the URL of the page where the form was displayed and submitted.

Q: How can I apply CSS styles to the contact form fields?

A: To modify the overall styles of the contact form fields and labels, add the needed styles in the “Customization area > Add Custom Styles” (at the bottom of the page that contains the list of forms):

  • Change the styles of all field labels:

fbuilder, #fbuilder label, #fbuilder span {

color: #00f;
}

  • Change the styles of all input and textarea fields:

fbuilder input[type=text], #fbuilder textarea, #fbuilder select {

border: 2px solid #00f;
}

  • Change the contact form submit button:

fbuilder .pbSubmit {

color: #00f;
font-weight: bold;
}

  • Change the contact form title and header description:

fbuilder .fform span {font-size:16px;}

To modify only a specific field in the contact form:

  • Step #1: In the contact form builder, click a field to edit its details and find the setting named “Add CSS Layout Keywords”.
  • Step #2: Add a class name into that field so the style specified in the CSS class will be applied to that field.
  • Step #3 (Note): Don’t add raw CSS rules directly in the form builder—enter only the name of a CSS class.
  • Step #4: Place the CSS class definition either into the “Customization area > Add Custom Styles” section, your theme’s CSS file, or wp-content/plugins/contact-form-to-email/css/stylepublic.css.

Examples: Add a class named specialclass into the setting “Add CSS Layout Keywords” and add one of these CSS rules:

  • For changing the field label:

    .specialclass label {
color: #00f;
}

  • For changing the input or textarea of the field:

    .specialclass input[type=text], .specialclass textarea, .specialclass select {
border: 2px solid #00f;
}

To see the modifications on the public contact form, you may need to refresh the page or clear the browser cache so old CSS styles aren’t loaded from cache.

Q: Are the forms GDPR compliant?

A: Yes. In all plugin versions, you can turn off IP tracking to avoid saving user IP data, and an “Accept terms / GDPR” field is available.

short_description: Contact form with visual form builder, database storage, CSV/Excel export, and direct email replies powered by a free AI assistant.
description:
Contact Form to Email features:

► Email delivery & notifications    
► Direct email reply with free AI assistant (no API key required)
► Saves messages into database
► Export to Excel / CSV
► Printable list of messages
► Visual drag and drop form builder 
► Anti-spam captcha 
► Field validation
► Printable reports
► One-click contact form
► Classic and AJAX submission available
► Automatic email reports
► Supports GDPR-compliant forms
► ... and more features (see below)

Contact Form to Email is a powerful and easy-to-use WordPress plugin to create contact forms, send their data to email addresses, and reply directly from the admin dashboard with AI assistance.

Contact Form to Email also saves the contact form data into a database, provides printable reports, and includes the option to export selected data to CSV/Excel files.

Contact Form to Email Main Features:

  • Direct Email Reply with AI Assistant: Reply to bookings and contact messages directly from the WordPress admin messages list. Includes a built-in, free AI assistant to automatically draft polite, context-aware responses in seconds—with no API key or external account required.
  • Email delivery / notifications: The contact form data is sent by email to one or more email addresses. It also supports configuring auto-replies to the user who filled out the contact form.
  • Form data saved into the database: Avoid losing submissions and keep a complete record of received contact form messages.
  • Printable list of messages: View the list of messages received from the contact form within a selected date range and print it.
  • Export data to CSV/Excel: Export contact form data to a standard format that can be used by other applications. Export email addresses and other contact form data using date and text search filters.
  • Automatic reports: Generate automatic reports of contact form usage and submitted data, including daily submission reports, cumulative hourly reports, and printable reports for specific fields to help you understand your data.
  • Automatic email reports: Send automatic reports to specified email addresses on a regular schedule.
  • Form validation: Set validation rules for each contact form field to keep your data clean.
  • Anti-spam protection: Built-in captcha anti-spam protection. No need to rely on external services for contact form anti-spam protection.
  • Drag and drop contact form builder: An intuitive contact form builder for customizing form fields and validation rules.
  • Customizable email messages: Specify the text of the contact form email notifications. Supports both plain text and HTML-formatted emails.
  • Multi-language support: The contact form builder allows you to enter field labels and validations in any language, with full support for special characters.
  • Classic and AJAX submission: After clicking the submit button, the user can be redirected to a “Thank You” page, or a “Thank You” message can be displayed on the same form page without refreshing it. This can be configured in the settings.
  • Enable/Disable notifications: Both email notifications to administrators and email confirmations to users can be optionally enabled or disabled from the settings area.

Contact Form to Email – More Features

There are also commercial versions of Contact Form to Email with additional features available at https://form2email.dwbooster.com/download

The commercial version can be converted into a payment form or booking form with integration for multiple payment gateways: PayPal Standard, PayPal Pro, Stripe, Authorize.net, Skrill, Mollie / iDEAL, TargetPay / iDEAL, SagePay, RedSys TPV, and Sage Payments. Payments are SCA-ready (Strong Customer Authentication) and compatible with the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2).

The commercial version also features an ultra-powerful visual form builder, file upload fields, conditional logic, multi-page forms, WooCommerce integration, Mailchimp integration, Clickatell and Twilio SMS integration, iCal attachments, signature fields for signing with a mouse or directly on touchscreens, and more.

Contact Form to Email Messages List

The messages list helps you review past contact form submissions, reply directly to users, and print or export records. It includes a search/filter form with the following options:

  • Search for: Search for specific text within the contact form messages.
  • From … To: Date range to include in the list and reports.
  • Item: If you have more than one contact form, select whether to view results from a specific contact form or from all forms.
  • Filter: Displays the list according to the selected filters and options.
  • Export to CSV: Exports the CSV data according to the selected filters and options.

Each message in the list includes quick action buttons:

  • Reply (with AI Assistant): Opens a reply modal pre-filled with the user’s email address and original submission. You can type brief instructions (e.g., “Confirm the booking for Tuesday at 10 AM”) and click Generate with AI to draft a complete reply using a free, keyless AI service. Sent replies are automatically appended to the message record for easy tracking.
  • Edit: Modify the stored submission data.
  • Delete: Remove individual or marked submissions.

The exported CSV file contains a header row with the field names, followed by one contact form submission per row, with one form field in each column. This allows you to easily import the data into other applications or select only the columns/fields you need (for example, selecting only email addresses). A CSV file can be opened and managed directly in Excel.

The list of contact form messages is shown below the search area. A Print button below the list formats the messages into a printer-friendly view.

The Contact Form Reports

The reports section lets you analyze the usage of your contact forms and the data entered into them. The first section contains a filter bar similar to the one on the messages list page. Below the filters, three graphical reports are available:

  • Submissions per day: Displays a line graph showing how many contact form submissions were received each day within the selected date range. This report can be used to evaluate contact form peaks and measure the impact of marketing campaigns.

  • Submissions per hour: Displays a line graph showing how many contact form messages were received during each hour of the day across all messages in the selected date range. This report helps identify peak hours so you can focus support resources accordingly.

  • Report of values for a selected field: Select any contact form field or metadata field (such as date, IP address, or hour) to see how many times each value has been entered or selected. This is very useful if your form is used as a poll to gather feedback, making it easy to generate reports on selectable fields and better understand your customers’ profiles and needs.

A Print button at the bottom of the page lets you print the value report for the selected contact form field in a printer-friendly format.

Automatic Email Reports

The Contact Form to Email plugin supports two types of automatic (periodic) email reports:

  • Global Email Reports: Configured below the list of forms. This option sends a report containing new submissions across all forms every specified number of days.

  • Form Email Reports: Configured on the settings page of each individual form. This option sends a report containing new submissions for that specific form every specified number of days.

Reports are attached as a CSV/Excel file to the emails. In both cases, you can specify the destination email addresses, email subject, email text, and report interval. More information is available in the “Other Notes” section.

Language Support

The Contact Form to Email plugin is compatible with all character sets. The troubleshoot area contains options to change the encoding of the plugin database tables if needed. Multiple translations are already included in the plugin.

Form Builder & AI-Assisted Replies

The plugin includes a visual drag-and-drop form builder to add, modify, and delete text fields, textareas, and email fields with their respective validations, plus an AI-assisted email reply system directly inside the bookings/messages list.
Replying to contact form messages with AI: Go to the “Messages” section and click the “Reply” button next to any submission. A modal window will open with the recipient’s email address and original message pre-loaded. You can optionally enter brief instructions in the AI Assistant Instructions box and click Generate with AI to automatically compose a response without needing an API key, then click Send Reply.

Opening the contact form messages in Excel: Go to either the “Reports” or “Messages” section and click the button labeled “Export to CSV”. CSV files can be opened in Excel—just double-click the downloaded CSV file, and it will display the selected contact form submissions, one per line.

Deleting a contact form message: Go to the “Messages” section and use the “Delete” button for the contact form message you want to delete. Each row in that list represents a contact form submission.

Getting the contact form email from the user: The “From” address used is a fixed email address specified in the contact form settings, which helps prevent emails from being classified as spam. However, when you click “Reply” in your email client, the user’s email address will appear automatically as the recipient because the Reply-To header is set for this purpose.

Customizing the captcha image: The captcha image used in the contact form is 100% implemented inside the plugin, so you don’t need to rely on third-party services or servers. In addition to the settings for customizing the captcha design, you can also replace the font files located in the contact-form-to-email/captcha/ folder.

Contact form email format: Notification emails sent from the contact form can be either plain-text or HTML emails. Plain-text emails are preferred in most cases since they are easier to edit and are more likely to pass anti-spam filters.

Contact form Clone button: The Clone button duplicates a complete contact form along with its settings. The contact form messages/emails and statistics are not duplicated.

Custom contact form submit button

There is a settings section in each form that allows you to specify the label of the submit button.

The class="pbSubmit" selector can be used to modify the button styles.

The styles can be applied in any of the CSS files of your theme or added in “Contact Form to Email > Customization area > Add Custom Styles” (at the bottom of the page that contains the list of forms).

For further modifications, the submit button is located at the end of the file cp-public-int.inc.php.

For general CSS style modifications and examples, check this FAQ entry: https://form2email.dwbooster.com/faq#q82

Customizing the automatic email reports

The settings for the email reports (both global and per-form reports) include the following configuration fields:

  • Enable Reports?: Option for enabling or disabling the reports.
  • Send report every: Indicate how often (in days) the reports will be sent.
  • Send after this hour (server time): Approximate time at which the reports will be sent, based on server time. Some site activity is needed to trigger report delivery, or you can set up a cron job for exact delivery timing.
  • Send email from: The “From” email address used for the reports. Avoid @aol.com and @hotmail.com “From” addresses to prevent anti-spam filtering issues.
  • Send to email(s): The list of email addresses (comma-separated) that will receive the reports.
  • Email subject: Subject of the email sent with the Contact Form to Email reports.
  • Email format?: Format of the email sent with the reports (HTML or Plain Text). In most cases, plain text is easier to set up and encounters fewer issues with anti-spam services.
  • Email Text (CSV file will be attached): Content of the email that will contain the Contact Form to Email reports. The reports will be attached in CSV format.

The contact form database

The messages received via the contact form are stored in the WordPress database table wp_cftemail_messages. You can export that data as automatic email reports or in CSV/Excel format from the messages list area. If needed, you can also query that table directly for further processing of the contact form data.

Importing messages

There is an option to import messages into the Contact Form to Email plugin, located below the messages list and labeled “Import CSV”.

Messages can be imported from a comma-separated CSV file: one record per line, one field per column. Do not use a header row with the field names.

The first 3 columns in the CSV file are the time, IP address, and email address. If you don’t have this information, leave the first three columns empty. After those initial columns, the fields (columns) must appear in the same order as in the form.

Sample format for the CSV file:

2013-04-21 18:50:00, 192.168.1.12, john@sample.com, "john@sample.com", "sample subject", "sample message"
2013-05-16 20:49:00, 192.168.1.24, jane.smith@sample.com, "jane.smith@sample.com", "other subject", "other message"

“From” address used for the emails

In the “Form Processing / Email Settings” section, the first setting is named Send email “From” and has the following options:

  • From fixed email address indicated below – Recommended option: If you select “From fixed…”, the customer’s email address will appear in the “To” address when you hit “Reply”. This is the recommended setting to avoid mail server restrictions.

  • From the email address indicated by the customer: If you select “From customer email”, the customer’s email will appear visually as the sender when you receive the email, but this is not supported by all hosting providers and can trigger spam filters, so it is not recommended in most cases.

The drag and drop contact form builder

The Form Builder lets you add, edit, and remove fields in the contact form and specify validation rules (required fields, email fields, etc.).

The following field types are currently available in the version published in the WordPress directory:

  • Single Line Text: Classic one-line text input.
  • Email: Validates that the email address has a valid format.
  • Paragraph Text: Classic multi-line (textarea) text input.

In other versions of the plugin, the following fields are also available: Numeric field with specific validations, Date-picker, Checkboxes, Multiple Choice Radio buttons, Dropdown / Select, Upload file fields, Password, Phone with specific validations, static texts, section breaks, and page breaks for multi-page contact forms.

Other features in the contact form builder:

  • Equal fields validation: Use it, for example, to confirm that the email or text typed in two different fields is identical. Valid for “Single Line Text” and “Email” fields.

  • Dependent fields: Use this feature to show/hide fields (any field type) based on the selection made in other fields (checkboxes, radio buttons, or select/drop-down fields). This feature isn’t fully available in this version since the related selection fields aren’t included.
